sourceGaps: The source is The Competition Problems from the International Chemistry Olympiads, Volume 3, edited by Anton Sirota, IUVENTA/IChO International Information Centre, Bratislava 2014. This is the collection edition of the 42nd IChO, 19–28 July 2010, Tokyo, Japan; it is not an obtained complete original competitor packet. The editorial preface explains normalized numbering and omissions of original grading points, selected practical grading graphs and data-dependent solution portions. Every procedure, chemical list, safety remark, native key and rubric actually printed in this section is retained.

Separate practical answer sheets/booklets and referenced visual-colorimetry answer tables are not supplied in this obtained volume section or as companions in the complete four-PDF IChO archive folder. The printed blank Part 3 identification form is retained. Competitor measurements are not invented.

Practical 1 references jury-approved percent-yield equations/graphs and a final NMR evaluation. Practical 2 references a distribution graph for marking measured heights. These missing graphs, unprinted equations and competitor spectra/measurements are not fabricated; all printed evaluation conditions and reference values are retained.

Teaching copying, distribution, transmission and adaptation are permitted by the printed Volume 3 notice with its required attribution. Commercial publication/distribution requires a waiver from the copyright holder. Attribution and the 2014 collection edition are retained; organizer hosting, commercially unrestricted use and completeness of the original 2010 packet are not claimed.

Only new physical pages 56–110 were personally read in this pass. Prior personal reading of common pages 1–6 is reused separately; no fresh common-page reading credit is claimed. Pages 111–291 remain unread/unclaimed, and the whole compilation queue remains unresolved.

sourceErrors.finding: The section cover prints “42th”, while all task/key page headers print 42nd, Tokyo, 2010. The historical cover spelling is documented; scientific metadata follows the printed task headers.

Key 1.3 prints 587.7·10^9 in its wavelength denominator, while its stated 3.380·10^-19 J answer and nanometre wavelength imply an inverse exponent. The printed positive exponent is retained and qualified.
The printed F step in 2.3 is NaCl(s)→Na(g)+Cl−(g), omitting the positive charge on Na. The equation is retained as printed with an explicit source note.
The key calls final titration volumes A and B cm³, then substitutes 0.0300 dm³ in both methods. The original unit-label discrepancy and complete alternatives are retained.
The s_free definition says HTAB in the free and complexed state, while the next s_complex definition separately denotes the complex. Both printed definitions are retained and qualified.
The evaluation specifies CDCl3 in conditions (ii)/(iii), then CHCl3 in condition (iv). Both native solvent labels are retained.
The Fe(III) formula subtracts c(Fe3+) from itself instead of the independently derived Fe(II) quantity. The exact printed formula is retained with an explicit source note, not silently repaired.
